rules: Every record remains a candidate until human review.
Similarity does not imply historical descent, common origin, or diffusion.
Publication and index dates are preserved separately; indexing novelty is not publication novelty.
Preprints are not peer-reviewed evidence and remain separately labeled.
Human remains and mortuary contexts require cultural-sensitivity review before public presentation.

new_candidates.title: Dataset to 'Rituals on the move? Unusual dietary habits among non-local elite female priestesses at the Hallstatt period cemetery of Modřice, Czech Republic'
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Provides δ13C, δ15N and 87Sr/86Sr data for 24 inhumations and 24 cremations plus fauna, water and plant baselines, creating a reusable observation layer for mobility/diet claims around a mortuary context.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: The dataset records isotopic observations; labels such as 'priestesses' and interpretations of status, ritual role or non-local identity require review of the associated study and archaeological context.

new_candidates.title: Intentional incisions on Neolithic Obsidian arrowheads from Central Anatolia: A techno-functional and iconographic approach
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Eleven newly identified incised obsidian arrowheads from Tepecik-Çiftlik expand the regional corpus and show deliberately variable markings with no fixed relation to raw material, production stage, typology or use-wear.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: The authors explicitly call for cautious interpretation. Shared marks may indicate a flexible cultural practice, but do not establish identity coding, symbolic meaning, descent, or diffusion.

new_candidates.title: On the origin of our fascination with crystals
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Experiments with enculturated chimpanzees found strong exploratory interest in crystals and identified transparency and geometric shape as salient attractors, providing a non-symbolic perceptual rival explanation for hominin crystal collection.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Chimpanzee attraction does not establish ancient hominin motives. The value for NOEMA is as an alternative mechanism that weakens any automatic crystal-object -> symbolic-thought inference.

new_candidates.title: Cultural affiliation accounts for most of the spatiotemporal variation in burial rite practices
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Uses mortuary data from approximately 4,200 individuals and ancestry/mobility data from more than 1,300 genomes across Western Eurasia ~10,000-2,000 BP; preliminary modeling reports cultural affiliation as the dominant predictor of burial orientation, with little ancestry effect.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: This is a bioRxiv preprint and must not be treated as peer-reviewed evidence. Cultural-affiliation variables, model structure and data harmonization require human methodological review before any NOEMA relationship or confidence update.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: Chimpanzee crystal attraction supplies a perceptual-salience explanation that does not require symbolic meaning.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Keep material attraction/salience separate from conventionalized symbolic use.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: Neolithic obsidian incisions are deliberate but variable and not tied to fixed production or use-wear patterns; authors caution against overclaiming identity function.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Code deliberate incision as observation; keep iconographic/identity interpretation as hypothesis.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: A large preprint analysis reports burial orientation tracking cultural affiliation more strongly than genomic ancestry.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Maintain ancestry, mobility, cultural affiliation and mortuary practice as competing/separable explanatory dimensions; await peer review.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: The Wiley chapter 'Demon Eaters and Bloody Charms' is dated 2026 in Crossref while the parent companion is marketed with 2027 publication metadata.
contradictions_or_pressure.action: Treat as possible ahead-of-print and require publication-status review.
